questions.stem: At Fernbrook, dashboards over a sensor table in an eventhouse almost always look at the last 14 days. Which policy keeps those days in fast storage?

options.text: A caching policy with a 14-day hot period

questions.explanation: The caching policy decides which data is hot: hot data is kept on local SSD for faster queries. A 14-day retention policy would delete everything older instead.

questions.stem: Readings older than three years must not be kept. Which setting handles that?
questions.explanation: The soft-delete period is how long data is guaranteed to stay available to query, measured from ingestion; after it, the data is removed, though not at an exact moment.

questions.stem: Every dashboard tile runs the same hourly aggregation over the whole sensor table. What makes those queries cheaper while keeping results current?

options.text: A materialized view over the aggregation

questions.explanation: Querying a materialized view is more performant than running the aggregation over the source table, and it returns an up-to-date result.

questions.stem: Which two changes follow the KQL query best practices for a query that looks for the word 'overheat' in the last day of messages?

options.text: Filter on time at the very end, after the other operators
Put the where on the datetime column first, right after the table
Use contains, because it matches whole words faster

questions.explanation: Predicates on datetime columns go first: their index can skip whole shards. For full terms, has works better than contains because it doesn't look for substrings.
